samples.summary: New yorkie-doc-store tests pass identically on the pre-change code — they guard a type-only change and cannot fail for the bug they cite
samples.evidence: The frontend hunk of this diff is purely type annotations/comments: `setCursorForHistory(pos)` stores the object by reference (`this.pendingCursorPos = pos`, yorkie-doc-store.ts:2882) and `recordHistoryPresence` publishes it as-is (`activeCursorPos: cursor`, line 2906). TypeScript narrowing to `{blockId, offset}` never strips properties at runtime, so `expect(store.getPresenceCursorPos()?.lineAffinity).toBe('forward')` (test line 422) and `expect(store.getPresenceCursorPos()).toEqual(pos)` (line 433) would have been green before the change too. The test comment claims it pins the runtime contract of the erasure the diff describes; in fact the erasure it claims to cover never existed at runtime here. The third test (Object.keys === ['blockId','offset']) is likewise unaffected by this diff.

samples.summary: The undo/redo presence-restore path that now carries lineAffinity has no test
samples.evidence: editor.ts undo (≈2030) and redo (≈2062) were changed from `cursor.moveTo({blockId, offset})` to `cursor.moveTo({...restoredPos, offset})` — a real behavior change (restored caret keeps its wrap-boundary reading). No test enters that branch: it is gated on `'getPresenceCursorPos' in docStore`, and grep shows `getPresenceCursorPos` exists only in packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts (plus its own test) — MemDocStore, used by every docs view test including the new caret-line-affinity.test.ts, has no such method (grep in packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts: no matches). The frontend store test only covers presence bookkeeping, not the editor's cursor restore. Duplicated code in two places, so both copies are untested.

samples.summary: scrollToPosition's switch from hardcoded 'backward' to pos.lineAffinity is untested
samples.evidence: `scrollToPosition` now resolves pixels with `pos.lineAffinity`, changing which visual line a jump-to-peer scroll targets. No test in packages/docs/test references scrollToPosition (grep for `scrollToPosition` matched only src/view/editor.ts, docs-view.tsx, docs-comments-controller.ts and the frontend store, no docs test files), and the new caret-line-affinity.test.ts does not call it.

samples.summary: resolvePositionPixel's new `undefined` → position.lineAffinity fallback is never distinguished by a test
samples.evidence: The new line `const affinity = lineAffinity ?? position.lineAffinity ?? 'backward'` documents that an omitted argument falls back to the position's own affinity. The only new caller-level coverage (caret-line-affinity.test.ts:199) goes through the peer path, which passes `peer.position.lineAffinity` — i.e. the argument and the fallback are always the same value, so the `??` chain is indistinguishable from the old signature. No test calls resolvePositionPixel with `undefined` while the position carries `lineAffinity: 'forward'` (packages/docs/test/view/peer-cursor.test.ts passes an explicit affinity in every case).

samples.summary: restoreLocalCursor now spreads the resolved position's affinity, but every existing test calls it without one
samples.evidence: The remote-change restore path was rewritten to `cursor.moveTo({...cursorPos, offset: ...})`. All call sites in tests pass affinity-free positions (table-link.test.ts:114/127/141/156/173, link-trailing-edge.test.ts:179/202, edit-link-in-place.test.ts:133/178/229/284), and the new caret-line-affinity.test.ts does not exercise restoreLocalCursor, so no test asserts that a resolved anchor's `lineAffinity` survives the round-trip onto the caret.

samples.summary: Wrap boundaries in the new test are produced by a proxied fake canvas context (measureText = length*6), so the boundary offsets are an artifact of the shim
samples.evidence: installCanvasShim returns a Proxy whose every unknown member is a no-op function and whose measureText is a fixed 6px/char. The tests then discover a 'real wrap boundary' via ArrowDown/Home under those synthetic metrics. This is a reasonable jsdom workaround and the assertions are still behavioral (affinity published, peer y-offsets differ), but the layout under test is entirely driven by mocked measurement, so a metrics-dependent affinity regression would not be caught.

verdict.reason: The behavior change is real and untested. editor.ts:2035-2038 (undo) and 2067-2070 (redo) now spread `...restoredPos` into `cursor.moveTo`, deliberately carrying `lineAffinity` through the presence restore. No test asserts that. Two frontend tests DO enter the `'getPresenceCursorPos' in docStore` branch with a real YorkieDocStore (editor-undo-selection.test.ts:98-118, editor-step-selection-font-size-undo.test.ts:103-147) — so the reviewer's sub-claim "no test enters that branch" is wrong — but those tests assert only getActiveSelection() (the separate restoreSelectionFromPresence path) and fontSize/undo-stack values; they pass identically if moveTo rebuilds `{blockId, offset}` and drops the affinity. All docs-package editor tests use MemDocStore, which has no presence methods (packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts: no matches for Presence), so they take the `else` branch entirely. The nearest coverage is store-level only (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:425-434 asserts getPresenceCursorPos() returns the affinity after undo; the concurrent integration test covers anchor/resolve) — neither exercises the editor's consumption. caret-line-affinity.test.ts contains no undo/redo at all. Under the test-adequacy rubric this is a clear behavior change with no meaningful test, duplicated in two code paths: major.
